A surrogate must represent an arbitrary local architecture including defects, track the irreversible material state over an unknown number of increments, remain stable when driven recursively by its own predictions, and fit within the memory available at every integration point. Here, a Composites World Model based on a Multi-Modal Spiking Transformer architecture is designed to meet these requirements. The proposed architecture combines a material encoder, a Spiking Neural Network memory block that tracks the long-term internal state of the material, and transformer blocks that learn the short-term applied strain state. The system is trained in three stages: material architecture encoding, base training on short time windows, and recursive fine-tuning with scheduled sampling to suppress cumulative error drift. The trained model is disassembled at inference and coupled to a non-linear FE solver, enabling structural scale simulation of composites containing embedded defects. Benchmarks against experimental results for IM7/8552 laminates under tension, compression and transverse shear, for pristine and wrinkled composites, show that the SNN memory block successfully tracks the material internal state and results in prediction errors between 0.4% and 4.8%.

title: Bayesian optimization on amortized search space
abstract: In real-world black-box optimization problems, a mechanistic simulator is often available that approximately predicts the behavior of the system as a function of the parameters being optimized. Here, we show how an amortized inverse map of such a simulator can be used in Bayesian optimization to restrict the search space while using a Gaussian process kernel that is aware of the original problem geometry. This allows for efficiently leveraging the low intrinsic dimensionality of the optimization problem. We characterize its approximation bias and information gain, and derive an intrinsic-dimension-dependent regret rate under additional geometric and Gaussian Process assumptions. We illustrate the method with an application to drug dosing personalization in Parkinson's disease. We use, as a simulator, a pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) model of a drug, a mechanistic model calibrated on population data with quantified parameter uncertainty. A dosing neural network is trained offline against the model, amortizing the map from patient PK/PD parameters to the regimen predicted to be optimal, and online Bayesian optimization then searches over this learned, low-dimensional representation rather than over raw dosages. Numerical simulations demonstrate the improved performance of our method in this application, as well as under simulator misspecification.

title: Two distinct notions of speed in antiferromagnets
abstract: The terahertz resonance frequencies of antiferromagnets characterize their precessional dynamics but do not necessarily imply faster laser-induced quenching of magnetic order. Here, we investigate the distinct roles of magnetic compensation and electronic scattering phase space by comparing ultrafast demagnetization in the antiferromagnetic charge-transfer insulator NiO, the metallic antiferromagnet Mn2Au, and a ferromagnetic Ni reference. The extracted response in Mn2Au is approximately four times faster than in NiO and substantially faster than in Ni. These observations are consistent with exchange-mediated scattering between antiparallel sublattices enabling rapid loss of antiferromagnetic order without requiring net angular-momentum transfer to an external reservoir, provided sufficient electronic scattering phase space is available. In insulating NiO, restricted electronic scattering channels reduces the ultrafast response. Our results distinguish ultrafast demagnetization from exchange-enhanced precession and identify the interplay of spin-flip probability and electronic scattering rate as a key factor governing the nonequilibrium response of compensated magnets.

title: From DNA Helicity to Structural Twist: An Undergraduate Laboratory Module for DNA Origami Design
abstract: Precise control of nanoscale architectures makes DNA origami a promising platform for biomedical applications such as drug delivery, biosensing, and bioimaging. A key constraint in DNA origami design is that crossover placement must account for the helical pitch of DNA. For new learners, however, it can be difficult to understand how a DNA helical pitch affects assembled structures. Here, we report a hands-on laboratory module to teach undergraduate students about this fundamental helical pitch/structure relationship.

title: Self-Consistent Induced Dipoles for MACE-POLAR in Molecular Embedding and Classical Dynamics
abstract: We couple the native Gaussian multipoles of MACE-POLAR-1-M to classical induced dipoles and compare the resulting solute densities, fields and forces with quantum references. The density-driven fixed point has a nonzero energy derivative with respect to its dipoles. An adjoint recovers forces on the converged surface to within 2.13 × 10−7 eV/Å of reconverged finite differences in twelve force-test configurations. A separate density comparison treats both partners quantum mechanically at twelve geometries of six small complexes.

title: Towards a Metrological Validation of PFAS Property Predictions by In-Context LLMs Across Four Architectures
abstract: In recent years, the use of large-language models (LLMs) as prediction tools has become increasingly popular. Despite this popularity, the metrological validation of LLMs in the study of chemical problems has been somehow neglected to date. To illustrate this need in chemistry, we introduce a minimal, metrologically grounded framework for validating in-context learning (ICL)-based prediction in LLMs on molecular physicochemical properties with reliable estimation of uncertainty.

title: Informatics-Driven Chemputation within the HERA Framework: Mathematical Modeling of Molecular State Entropy, Reaction-Diffusion Flow Kinetics, and Closed-Loop Bayesian Optimization
abstract: The integration of physical chemical synthesis with digital information networks remains bottlenecked by the lack of unified frameworks for lossless molecular state serialization, secure long-range telemetry, and automated robotic re-materialization. This study introduces the HERA framework, a comprehensive model that converts chemical supply chains into executable digital information routing problems.

title: AMBER2LAMMPS: Validated conversion of AMBER-family topologies to LAMMPS
abstract: AMBER topology files encode a complete molecular-mechanics model rather than only molecular connectivity. Translating them to LAMMPS requires preservation of bonded parameters, charges, Lennard-Jones coefficients, exclusions, topology-specific 1–4 scaling, masses, and periodic-cell semantics. AMBER2LAMMPS is an open-source Python package that converts one or more fully parameterized AMBER topology templates and matching PDB coordinates to LAMMPS data and parameter files.

title: Linear-Algebraic Audit of Biomedical Matrices: Five Empirical Case Studies in Regularized Inference
abstract: High-throughput biomedical assays—ranging from gene expression microarrays to mass spectrometry and clinical registries—routinely exhibit severe rank deficiency (N ≪ P ), zero-inflation, and extreme sample outliers. Standard chemometric and bioinformatics pipelines apply variance auto-scaling, simplex normalization, and bilinear projections (PCA/PLS-DA) without verifying operator conditioning or modal localization.

title: Direct Access to 5-Aryl-2-Pyrones via Palladium-Catalyzed Decarbonylative Cross-Coupling of Coumalic Acid
abstract: The selective synthesis of 5-substituted 2-pyrones remains challenging despite their synthetic potential. Herein, we report a palladium-catalyzed decarbonylative Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling of simple coumalic acid, providing direct access to 5aryl-2-pyrones in up to 58% yield. Enabled by DPEphos, the transformation accommodates diverse arylboronic acids while preserving the reactive heterocyclic framework.

title: A Convenient One-Pot Route to [Thianthrenium][B(C 6 F 5 ) 4 ]
abstract: One-electron oxidants paired with weakly coordinating anions are indispensable for accessing reactive cations. The thianthrenium radical cation, [TA] •+ (TA = thianthrene), is a strong outer-sphere oxidant (E 1/2 ≈ +0.8 V vs ferrocene/ferrocenium) whose neutral by-product is easily removed, and its [B(C 6 F 5 ) 4 ] − salt ( 1 ) has been used in organometallic, rare-earth, and porphyrin chemistry. Existing preparations often rely on nitrosonium oxidation or salt metathesis in liquid SO 2 , which is challenging to handle, or MeCN, where traces may be deleterious to subsequent reaction steps.

title: Correlative Stimulated Raman Scattering Microscopy and Nano-DESI Mass Spectrometry Imaging for Mapping Isomeric Triglycerides in Lipid Droplets in Biological Tissues
abstract: Lipid droplets (LDs) are key organelles involved in lipid storage and metabolic regulation. Triglycerides (TGs) are the major component of LDs’ neutral lipid core. Alterations in TG composition are associated with different biological states or disease conditions, yet spatially resolved analysis of TG isomers in biological tissues remains challenging. Here, we present a correlative multimodal imaging strategy that integrates stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) microscopy with high-resolution nanospray desorption electrospray ionization (nano-DESI) isomer selective mass spectrometry imaging…

title: Two-carbon annulation of primary amines to azetidines
abstract: Azetidines are valuable motifs in medicinal chemistry, yet their broader use is constrained by a lack of general, concise methods for preparing N–H azetidines from simple feedstocks. Here, we report a direct two-carbon annulation of unprotected primary alkylamines that provides α-mono- and α,α-disubstituted azetidines. Dual photoredox and hydrogen-atomtransfer catalysis enables α-C–H alkylation with vinylsulfonium reagents to generate γ-amino sulfonium intermediates, which undergo intramolecular SN2 cyclization to forge the fourmembered ring without protecting groups or prefunctionalization.

title: Limited Intrinsic CO2/CH4 Selectivity in Imine-Linked COF-LZU-1: Evidence from PBE-D3 Adsorption Energetics and Binary-Mixture Monte Carlo Simulations
abstract: Imine-linked covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are widely proposed for CO2/CH4 separation, yet the intrinsic selectivity of the archetypal framework COF-LZU1 has not been quantified against a transparent baseline. Here, periodic PBE-D3 calculations and grand canonical Monte Carlo (GCMC) simulations are combined to test whether pristine COF-LZU1 discriminates between CO2 and CH4.

title: Benzylsuccinate synthase as an engineerable platform for stereoselective C–C bond formation via C–H functionalization
abstract: Stereoselective olefin hydroalkylation offers a direct route to chiral C(sp3)-rich products from simple C–H substrates, but biocatalytic platforms for this transformation are rare. Glycyl radical enzymes catalyze hydroalkylation in anaerobic metabolism, yet applications in chemical synthesis have been precluded by a lack of methods for in vitro activation. Here we use a soluble activase to unlock GRE hydroalkylases as a tunable class of radical biocatalysts.

title: Exploring Boltzmann Distributions via Kernel-Based Fokker–Planck Ensemble Transport
abstract: Local trajectory-based samplers can relax within a visited basin long before finite trajectories cross barriers to other Boltzmann-relevant regions. We introduce the Fokker–Planck Transformer (FPT), a training-free interacting-ensemble method that makes the instantaneous ensemble distribution a dynamical variable, shifting exploration from trajectory-wise barrier crossing toward distribution-level redistribution. FPT discretizes the current-velocity representation of overdamped Fokker–Planck evolution by combining energetic drift with a kernel estimate of the ensemble score.

title: Spacer accommodation under geometric confinement governs phase behavior in mixed Ruddlesden–Popper and Dion–Jacobson halide perovskites
abstract: Mixing organic spacers broadens the structural diversity of two-dimensional (2D) halide perovskites (HPs); however, predicting whether chemically distinct spacers can be incorporated into a shared layered phase remains a significant challenge. Here, we integrate high-throughput compositional screening and diffraction-based phase mapping with molecular dynamics simulations accelerated by machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIP-MD) to investigate combinations of five Dion–Jacobson (DJ) spacers with varying alkyl-chain lengths and three aliphatic or aromatic Ruddlesden–Popper (RP) spacers.

title: QM/MM Simulations Reveal Differences in Hydrolysis Mechanisms of Ertapenem and Faropenem in L1 Metallo-β-Lactamase Leading to Different Product Binding Modes
abstract: L1, a class B3 metallo-β-lactamase (MBL) from Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, efficiently hydrolyzes most β-lactam antibiotics and evades β-lactamase inhibitors, both clinically available and those in late-stage trials targeting other MBLs. Detailed understanding of the L1 mechanism is necessary to design effective inhibitors. Building on our previous quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) study of L1catalyzed hydrolysis of the penem antibiotic faropenem, we here investigate hydrolysis of a 1β-methyl carbapenem (ertapenem) using MM and enhanced sampling QM/MM MD simulations at the DFTB3…

title: HFn-E2: a computationally designed human H-ferritin nanocage codelivering iron and the covalent GPX4 inhibitor ML210 for ferroptosis induction in lung cancer — design, PBPK scenario modelling, structure validation and human-data premise analysis
abstract: Ferroptosis induction by covalent inhibition of glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) is a validated anticancer mechanism, but the most potent chemotype — the masked nitrile-oxide inhibitor ML210 — has never been formulated in a protein nanocage, and single-agent iron delivery is insufficient on its own. We present HFn-E2, a computationally designed human H-ferritin (HFn) cage intended to codeliver a mineralised iron core (target 1,000–2,000 Fe/cage) and ML210 (20–50/cage; Fe:ML210 ≈ 20:1–100:1) to transferrin receptor 1 (TfR1)-positive lung tumours, releasing both payloads upon lysosomal cage…

title: Diastereoselective synthesis of 3-monosubstituted phthalides through the MCR of phthalaldehydic acid, sulfoxonium ylides and thiols
abstract: A Brønsted acid-catalyzed multicomponent reaction (MCR) of phthalaldehydic acids, stabilized sulfoxonium ylides, and thiols is developed for the synthesis of 3-monosubstituted phthalides, a structural motif of considerable relevance to natural product and medicinal chemistry. The reaction proceeds under mild conditions and a ords the desired phthalide products featuring a thiol-functionalized side-chain in moderate to good yields with excellent anti-diastereoselectivity.

title: LabSense: A Digital Workflow for Measuring and Reducing Resource Consumption in Research Labs
abstract: Laboratory science carries a disproportionately large environmental footprint, driven by intensive energy use, reliance on singleuse plastics, hazardous waste generation, and resource-heavy infrastructure, despite widespread desire among researchers to operate more sustainably. Yet many scientists lack the data needed to identify where to begin or which interventions would be most effective.

title: On parallel and sequential mass spectrometry
abstract: Many emerging frontiers in biological mass spectrometry, including comprehensive single-cell proteomics and ultra-low-input proteomics and metabolomics, are now constrained less by ion formation than by how efficiently instruments capture, route, and analyze ion flux from scarce and complex samples. In modern workflows, this flux is continuous and information-rich, yet only a fraction is recorded. As sample complexity rises, congestion and undersampling increase, lowerabundance species are preferentially missed, and information yield may plateau or even decline.

title: Methods for Expanding the NIST Mass Spectral Library with Highly Relevant Compounds
abstract: For over 40 years, the NIST Mass Spectral Library has served as the most authoritative source of reference quality mass spectra, used by thousands of labs to confidently identify chemical compounds. However, improvement of the library relies not only on expanding its size but also on increasing its relevance. To achieve this, a cheminformatic workflow was developed to facilitate the selection of chemical compounds that are maximally relevant across the numerous, often disparate disciplines and industries that rely on the library.

title: Materials, manufacturing and sensing mechanisms of midinfrared photonic sensors
abstract: Mid-infrared (MIR) photonic sensors offer chip-scale access to molecular fingerprint spectroscopy for label-free detection of gases, chemicals, and biomolecules. Despite rapid progress in MIR materials, waveguides, resonators, sources and detectors, translating integrated MIR sensors into reproducible, calibrated instruments remains challenging. We examine how fabrication variability and component integration constrain the translation of device performance into reliable sensing.

title: Effect of Thermochemical Treatments on the Ethanol Yields from Taro Stalks
abstract: Taro stalks (Colocasia esculenta) were evaluated as a renewable lignocellulosic feedstock for bioethanol production. Three pretreatment methods—hydrothermal, dilute acid, and alkaline-peroxide—were used to release fermentable sugars. The effects of pretreatment solid loading (5–20% m/v) and sulfuric acid concentration (0.25–1.0% v/v) on hydrolysate fermentability were then assessed. While ethanol yields were comparable across pretreatments at 10% m/v solid loading, significant differences were observed in the total solids of the hydrolysates.

title: A 2% drift-tube window resolves skeleton length, not the PFOS isomers summed in serum
abstract: Suspect identification often treats two ions as one structure when their drift-tube collision cross sections agree within 2%. We asked what structural change that window can finish, pairing same-formula ions in the ToxCast drift-tube library, scoring each pair by the change in heavy-atom graph diameter, and treating each reported cross section as one draw with a 0.52 Å2 measurement scale. We then tested the rule against the ten measured perfluorooctanesulfonate (PFOS) isomers, the 89 PFOS connectivities in the U.S.

title: Nanogel structure shapes host-cell interactions and antibiotic performance against biofilm-associated and intracellular Staphylococcus aureus
abstract: Antibiotic treatment is often compromised by bacterial persistence within biofilms and host cells, contributing to recurrent infections and antimicrobial resistance.Here, a structurally diverse series of N-isopropylacrylamide (NIPAM)-based nanogels (NGs) is evaluated to deliver ceftiofur (CF) against Staphylococcus aureus , using bovine mastitis as a clinically relevant context. Surface chemistry and network architecture are varied to determine how NG structure influences biological interactions and antibiotic performance.

title: Selective Lanthanide-Binding Peptides: Molecular Insights into Binding Affinity and Selectivity
abstract: Rare earth elements (REEs), including the lanthanides, are essential to clean-energy technologies, semiconductors, electric vehicles, turbines, and other advanced materials that exploit their luminescent, magnetic, and catalytic properties. Current REE separation methods, however, suffer from poor selectivity, high solvent use, and environmental burden, which motivates greener and more selective strategies.

title: Structural and Electronic Origins of Ceria with Versatile Functionality: From Three-Way Catalysis to Chemical Mechanical Polishing and Actinide Surrogacy
abstract: With the rapid growth of the global rare-earth industry, high-abundance cerium-based functional materials, particularly CeO2 and its derivatives, have become essential in diverse applications, including automotive three-way catalysis, precision chemical-mechanical polishing, and actinide surrogate studies. However, the fundamental structural and electronic origins underlying the unique versatility of CeO2 remain incompletely understood.

title: Network Valence Dictates Gelation Pathway and Viscoelasticity in Reversibly Bonded TetraPEG
abstract: Theory predicts that reversibly bonded star polymers can undergo liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) or form single-phase equilibrium gels depending on the polymer concentration and the bond equilibrium constant. To explore these possible phase behaviors, this work examines four-armed poly(ethylene glycol) star polymers (tetraPEGs) with transient boronate ester bonds and finds that they exhibit only a single-phase sol-gel transition. Bulk rheology shows that the bond equilibrium constant in the hydrogel, K gel , is directly related to the sol-gel boundary.

title: ICPoly: An Automated Molecular Dynamics Workflow for Characterizing Structure, Dynamics, and Transport in Polymer Ion-Exchange Membranes
abstract: Predicting ionic transport in polymer ion-exchange membranes requires molecular models that connect polymer structure and hydration with local dynamics and collective charge transport. Here, we present ICPoly, an automated molecular dynamics workflow for characterizing the structure, dynamics, and ionic conductivity of these membranes. ICPoly integrates sequence-controlled polymer construction and fragment-based GAFF2 parameterization with staged classical and machine-learned equilibration, molecular-connectivity monitoring, and color-field nonequilibrium molecular dynamics (NEMD).

title: Effect of Cu(II) Complexation on the Anticancer Activity of Zidovudine in the NCI-60 Human Tumor Cell Line Screen
abstract: Zidovudine (AZT, azidothymidine) was originally synthesized as a potential anticancer agent. Originally synthesized in 1964 by Jerome Horwitz at the Michigan Cancer Foundation during efforts to develop antitumor nucleoside analogues, AZT demonstrated insufficient anticancer activity in early evaluations and was not pursued further at that time. Despite its clinical success as an antiviral agent, AZT has continued to attract interest in its anticancer properties, including inhibition of telomerase activity, induction of DNA damage, modulation of cell-cycle progression, and disruption of…

title: Spartan: Design and Recent Advances of a Molecular Modeling Program for Maximum Produc vity in Research and Educa on
Chemoenzymatic Synthesis of Quillaic Acid, the Terpenoid Aglycone of QS-21
abstract: Quillaic acid is the aglycone of QS-21, a triterpenoid saponin that has been clinically evaluated as an immunoadjuvant. Current access to quillaic acid has so far been limited to isolation from natural sources or semisynthesis from minimally-oxidized oleanane precursors, which limits the range of modifications that can be performed on the pentacyclic skeleton. In the same vein, previous total syntheses of oleanane triterpenoids have largely relied on cascade polyene cyclization, which will be difficult to implement on quillaic acid due to its functional group arrangements.

title: The Huc hydrogenase maintains catalytically active states in air using a high-potential iron-sulfur relay and internal electron transfer
abstract: Huc is a membrane-associated [NiFe]-hydrogenase that inputs electrons from trace levels of H 2 into the aerobic respiratory chain of Mycobacterium smegmatis . Unlike most hydrogenases, Huc is catalytically active in air, yet it still can form the typically inactive Ni-B state. How it maintains catalytic turnover despite accessing this inactive state is unknown. Here, we use EPR spectroscopy to determine the oxidation state and relative reduction potentials of the metallocofactors in Huc.

title: Interference-Driven Loss of Spectral Specificity in Long-Wavelength NIR Lactate Sensing in Complex Media.
abstract: Continuous lactate monitoring is valuable for managing peritoneal dialysis in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD), where lactate acts both as a marker of dialysis efficacy and an early indicator of sepsis. Existing monitoring approaches are intermittent and invasive. Long-wavelength near-infrared (LWNIR) spectroscopy enables the possibility of non-invasive, real-time lactate sensing, but its translation has been hindered by calibration instability and reduced spectral specificity in complex biological media.

title: In Situ Polymerized Main/Side-Chain Bifluorinated Cross-Linked Polyether Electrolytes for High-Voltage Lithium Metal Batteries
abstract: Polyether electrolytes are compelling candidates for lithium metal batteries owing to their high ionic conductivity and conformal interfacial contact. However, their widespread adoption is impeded by inherent vulnerabilities, including limited oxidative stability against high-voltage cathodes, uncontrolled lithium dendrite growth, and persistent interfacial side reactions.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: momipy: A time-resolved momentum microscopy data analysis workflow
abstract: Photoemission momentum microscopy is an emerging approach to photoelectron spectroscopy that is transforming electronic band structure mapping at both laboratory-based and large-scale facilities. Its extension to time-resolved measurements has recently enabled major advances, ranging from the femtosecond imaging of exciton wavefunctions to dark-field photoelectron microscopy of light-induced dynamics and strong light-matter interactions. However, the rapid acquisition of high-dimensional data sets (including electron in-plane momenta $k_x$ and $k_y$, kinetic energy $E_\mathrm{kin}$, time $Δt$, and more) poses substantial challenges for data handling and analysis. A typical workflow encompasses data acquisition, exploratory visualization, calibration and targeted feature extraction, with data management ideally guided by FAIR principles. Here, we present momipy, a Python package that streamlines the momentum microscopy data analysis workflow efficiently and at low computational cost. Among other features, momipy provides interactive 4D data visualization, energy and momentum calibration, space-charge correction, and a broad selection of multidimensional data analysis routines, including binning, momentum-map extraction and time-, energy- and momentum-resolved model fitting. momipy is accompanied by a selection of interactive example scripts, supporting adoption of momipy by both experienced researchers and users new to momentum microscopy.

title: Whose Risks Count? What 1,901 AI Incidents Reveal About Corporate Disclosures
abstract: AI systems can harm people, yet the AI actors that provide or deploy them are rarely obliged to disclose these risks. US securities regulation is an exception. Companies registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) must disclose their material risks, including those of their AI systems, in filings that carry liability for misstatement. Materiality, however, is defined by what a reasonable investor would consider important, so harms to third parties enter disclosure only insofar as they become financial risks for the company. We test whether AI harms do so by matching 9,001 AI incidents to 18,229 SEC filings of 328 AI actors by risk type. Of the 1,901 incidents with filings before and after them, half belong to a risk type that the AI actor never disclosed, and this share varies with the kind of harm. Filings disclose the risk types of 67\% of system failures but only 2\% of social system harms, and AI actors themselves report fewer than 2\% of incidents. Securities disclosure thus records the risks that AI actors face rather than the harms that people subject to AI bear. Public authorities that hold AI actors accountable for such harms could make them financially material. We release DISC, the Disclosure--Incident Securities Corpus, to support this work.

title: Witnessing Molecular Conformation via Optical Cycling Centers
abstract: Molecular conformation plays a central role in determining molecular properties and dynamics. Here, we report the production and conformer-resolved spectroscopy of cold calcium 3-hydroxyphenoxide radical (CaOC$_6$H$_4$-3-OH) in a cryogenic buffer-gas cell. Internal rotation of the hydroxyl group gives rise to distinct $anti$- and $syn$-conformers. The CaO moiety acts as an optical cycling center (OCC), enabling the $\widetilde A - \widetilde X$ and $\widetilde B - \widetilde X$ transitions of both conformers to be resolved by laser-induced fluorescence spectroscopy. Dispersed fluorescence measurements reveal diagonal vibrational branching fractions of 0.91-0.93, indicating favorable optical cycling characteristics. Following excitation of off-diagonal vibronic transitions near the calculated torsional barrier in the $\widetilde A$ state, the emission remains predominantly conformer specific, indicating that conformational identity is largely preserved over the excited-state fluorescence lifetime. These results demonstrate that a metal-centered OCC can serve as an intrinsic, site-specific optical reporter of molecular conformation, providing a foundation for repetitive optical readout and studies of conformational dynamics at the single-molecule level.

title: Precise experimental investigation of the reflection properties caused by s-polarized evanescent waves and the Casimir puzzle
abstract: We report a high-precision experiment on measuring the low-frequency magnetic field reflected from a metallic plate. This experiment is designed to give insight into why theoretical predictions of the fundamental Lifshitz theory using the standard response function to the electromagnetic waves are in contradiction with the data of numerous precision measurements of the Casimir force (the Casimir puzzle). To attain these ends, we measured the magnitude and phase of the lateral component of the magnetic field produced by an oscillating magnetic dipole and reflected from a metallic plate. These quantities are completely determined by the evanescent waves with the transverse electric (s) polarization. The obtained measurement data are compared with theoretical predictions using the standard Drude response function of the metal to the low-frequency electromagnetic waves. It is shown that there are both quantitative and qualitative disagreements with these predictions, so that in the region of low-frequency s-polarized evanescent waves the Drude response function is excluded by the data. Keeping in mind that just the s-polarized evanescent waves are responsible for the Casimir puzzle, our results highlight the causes for its emergence. It is emphasized that, in addition to the Casimir effect, searching for the adequate nonlocal response functions of metals to the evanescent waves is of utmost significance for many areas of physics as near-field optical microscopy, nanophotonics, surface plasmon polaritons, radiative heat transfer, and others.

title: Helices at Twisted Ferroelectric Interfaces
abstract: We report that twisted interfaces, formed between two ferroelectric lithium niobate single crystals, contain arrays of coherently bonded and elastically deformed nanoscale structural helices, separated from one another by screw dislocations. The helices generate remarkable contrast in four dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D STEM) and through related differential phase contrast (DPC). Such images have been successfully rationalised by modelling the trajectory of electrons that channel along helical pathways as they traverse the interface, but the structural helices implied have also been directly imaged using electron ptychography. Importantly, as lithium niobate is a uniaxial ferroelectric, the torsional strain in these structural helices necessarily also causes dipolar helices to form, inferred through consideration of pertinent piezoelectric tensors and flexoelectric coefficients. Helices are topologically distinct from the more commonly reported vortices and, importantly, they are chiral. Helical (and hence chiral) character was confirmed by observing that DPC images were identical before and after the sample was inverted. Chirality was also established through second harmonic optical circularly-polarised dichroism measurements, in which unusually large interfacial signals were seen. It must be stressed that the arrays of helices observed are distinct from moiré patterns; they facilitate lattice rotation combining plastic and elastic deformation and are not simply a superposition of lattices, twisted with respect to one another. Thus, intimately bonded twisted oxide interfaces will have distinctly different characteristics from those of twisted stacks of two-dimensional van der Waals materials, opening up a new and distinct kind of twistronics.

title: Nanoparticle transport and retention in tumours
abstract: Mathematical modelling and systematic studies in mouse tumour models uncover pathophysiological features and nanoparticle design criteria that promote tumour retention, providing cues and clues for improving the efficacy of cancer nanotherapy.

title: Perfumer: A Large Language Model-based Agentic Framework Accelerating Structural Relaxation and Electronic Band Prediction for First-Principle Calculation
abstract: First-principles structural relaxation and band calculations require substantial computation and expertise. Here we present Perfumer, a large language model-based agentic framework that couples Quantum ESPRESSO with two predictive models. Across tested structures, pre-relaxation with Perfumer-relax model followed by QE refinement yielded a 2.75-fold overall speedup over QE alone. Perfumer-band model combines a periodic graph neural network with a latent Hermitian spectral head returns 12 band energies at any requested wavevector, preserving reciprocal lattice periodicity and time-reversal symmetry without constructing Hamiltonian. Trained on 125,153 self-curated band structures, Perfumer-band model reaches a median per-material mean absolute error of 0.157 eV on 2,607 test materials, including lanthanide, actinide and magnetic compounds, from held-out composition families spanning 85 elements, taking about 97 ms per material on two consumer CPU cores. The agent turns natural-language requests into relaxation-to-band workflows, from a single uploaded structure to automatically constructed new candidates and returns predicted properties.

title: Learning from Context: Leave-One-Out Prediction in Jump Diffusions
abstract: Continuous diffusion models generate discrete data through stochastic dynamics in an embedding space. We consider jump diffusions that additionally reset coordinates to embeddings of categorical values. A coordinate's own corrupted state can make prediction easy, potentially reducing the pressure to learn dependencies between coordinates. We study leave-one-out (LOO) prediction, in which each coordinate is predicted from the corrupted states of the other coordinates. We show that, under stated assumptions, jump diffusions with complete coordinate resets and state-independent clocks preserve the prescribed marginals when reset destinations use exact LOO probabilities and the drift uses the full endpoint posterior. We further show that this drift can be constructed from LOO probabilities by analytic likelihood completion without additional network evaluations. We evaluate unrestricted, LOO, and completed predictions on Text8 and LM1B text generation and ZINC250k molecular graph generation. LOO-based variants improve key generation metrics over matched unrestricted controls on all three datasets. Controlled interventions assess reliance on local inputs and context, and we analyze the effect of analytic likelihood completion.

title: From Benchmarks to the Bench: Preference, Correspondence and Selectivity in Bidirectional Drug-Target Screening
abstract: Identifying active molecules for known targets and potential targets for existing drugs is central to drug discovery and repurposing. Drug-target interaction (DTI) models can rank vast numbers of drug-target pairs, but limited experimental capacity restricts testing to a small number of candidates. We compared the bidirectional recommendations of 13 released systems across 711 molecular structures of FDA-approved drugs and 614 human proteins. For the same target or drug, pairs of models produced completely disjoint Top-10 molecule and protein lists in 77.8% and 70.1% of comparisons, respectively. Even where recommendations overlapped, agreement between some systems largely reflected recurring preferences for the same candidates. Published inhibition measurements for 79 molecules and 65 kinases revealed that some systems enriched active candidates, yet their hit yields changed little when recommendations were matched to different drugs or targets, whereas other systems lost substantially more hits. Some of the former systems also rarely ranked both molecules and kinases correctly when two drugs favoured different kinases. We further retrained the same architecture on the same data, with the training objective fixed and random seeds varied. Despite similar test performance, mean pairwise Top-10 overlap on a separate screening catalogue was about two candidates. Our study moves DTI model evaluation beyond benchmark performance to assess whether model predictions can guide meaningful experimental decisions in drug discovery and target identification.

title: Evidence from a Multi-Regime Causal Discovery Benchmark: UCMT Algorithms, Comparative Performance, and Controlled Ablation Studies
abstract: We present an internal, pre-registered evaluation of the UCMT causal discovery algorithm family alongside established alternatives across heterogeneous benchmark regimes, complemented by a separately pre-registered, controlled study of UCMT v2 Global components. The contribution is both empirical and methodological: a family-stratified comparison of three actively developed algorithm configurations and targeted evidence about which internal stages affect their outcomes. In the main benchmark, UCMT v2 Global has higher directed F1 than NOTEARS and DAGMA in selected real, semi-synthetic and Gaussian-network comparisons at the paired-run level, while trailing leading permutation-search methods in other settings. The BOSS-based UCMT v4 produces a CSuite-specific directed-F1 improvement over BOSS (mean paired difference +0.279; pair-level Holm p < 0.001), but the dataset-level adjusted result is not significant (p = 0.188). In a separate fixed-skeleton ablation, UCMT v2 Global exceeds an adapted R^2-SortnRegress orientation baseline on standardized iSCM data (directed F1 0.537 vs 0.468, dataset-level Holm p = 0.031); absolute orientation accuracy is 0.563 and there is no established broad advantage over RESIT, ANM or DirectLiNGAM. Controlled ablations show that sparsity and BIC-based refinement materially affect some outcomes, whereas the examined arbitration and automatic regime-selection mechanisms do not yield confirmed general improvements. We report performance shortcomings, multiple-testing correction, runtime costs, evaluation limitations and reproducibility checks. The results support UCMT as an implemented and empirically investigated algorithm family, not a claim of overall superiority, independent validation or demonstrated commercial impact.

title: Feasibility of methionine oxidation quantification in proteins through Raman and FT-IR spectroscopy
abstract: The development of biopharmaceuticals poses unique challenges, with alterations of chemical integrity potentially impairing product efficacy and safety. Thus, oxidation-susceptibility of drug candidates is typically assessed by chromatographic methods, potentially coupled with mass spectrometry (LC-MS), which enable residue-specific oxidation monitoring but require high-resolution instrumentation, specialized expertise, and may introduce sample preparation artefacts. These constraints have raised interest in orthogonal, simple and fast methods to probe oxidation in native protein samples.

title: Machine Learning-Assisted Raman Spectroscopy for Quantitative Prediction of Multicomponent Mixtures
abstract: Machine Learning (ML)-assisted Raman spectroscopy that can efficiently analyze molecularly specific fingerprints is well suited for quantitative analysis of complex chemical mixtures. However, developing accurate predictive ML models for multicomponent systems remains difficult because collecting sufficient experimental calibration data is slow, expensive, and limited. In this work, we present a ML-assisted Raman spectroscopy framework for predicting the quantitative composition of multicomponent lipid mixtures (consisting of 15 lipids).

title: Lipid nanoparticle-delivered Cas13b ribonucleoproteins targeting survivin overcome gemcitabine resistance in pancreatic cancer
abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains one of the deadliest cancers, largely due to its poor response to chemotherapy and the development of drug resistance. Survivin (BIRC5), an inhibitor of apoptosis frequently overexpressed in PDAC, contributes to tumor cell survival and gemcitabine resistance, making it an attractive therapeutic target. Here, we developed a lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-based platform for the delivery of preassembled spCas13b ribonucleoproteins (RNPs) to achieve transient and sequence-specific RNA silencing in pancreatic cancer cells. We optimized ionizable lipid formulations for Cas13b RNP encapsulation and identified a formulation achieving approximately 80% encapsulation efficiency, with sustained colloidal stability and gene-silencing activity during seven days of storage at 4{degrees}C. LNP-delivered Cas13b RNPs efficiently silenced endogenous BIRC5 in three pancreatic cancer cell lines, reducing survivin protein levels and inducing apoptosis. In gemcitabine-resistant PANC-1 cells, BIRC5 silencing synergistically enhanced the cytotoxic effect of gemcitabine in vitro. This therapeutic combination was further evaluated in a PANC-1 xenograft model, where only the combined administration of BIRC5-targeting Cas13b RNP-LNPs and gemcitabine significantly inhibited tumor growth, without apparent systemic toxicity. Intratumoral administration also restricted nanoparticle distribution to the injected tumors. These findings establish LNP-mediated delivery of Cas13b RNPs as a new strategy for transient RNA-targeted therapy and provide proof of concept for combining survivin silencing by Cas13b with chemotherapy to address gemcitabine resistance in pancreatic cancer.

title: Enhancing Grignard Reactions via Anion Borrowing in Deep Eutectic/Organic Biphasic Media
abstract: The rational optimization of the Grignard reaction remains a considerable challenge for synthetic chemists. Deep eutectic solvents (DESs) have emerged as powerful reaction media to enhance nucleophilic additions to unsaturated organic molecules. In this protocol, a solution of the Grignard in THF is added to the DES containing the substrate under vigorous stirring. In this study, we determine the underlying causes for this beneficial effect by combining ab initio molecular dynamics, QM/MM simulations, and enhanced sampling, using i-PrMgCl and acetophenone as reagents, THF as the organic solvent, and a 1:2 solution of choline chloride:glycerol as the DES. Our results demonstrate enhanced chemoselectivity for the Grignard addition over β-H transfer side reaction from the isopropyl group when in DES/THF. This enhanced selectivity stems from the formation of chlorinated dimagnesium entities at the DES interface. While the neutral Grignard species in neat THF kinetically favors β-H transfer, chloride enrichment from the DES renders both pathways kinetically competitive and markedly increases the thermodynamic preference for the addition product through enhanced intramolecular stabilizing interactions. This is in line with experimental evidence of increased selectivity in the presence of various halide salts. This mechanistic interpretation paves the way for the rational improvement of Grignard reagents, allowing an even broader application of these compounds in these nonconventional solvents.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Improving hydrogen production from water can support abundant global crops
abstract: Water, at least in its purest form, contains hydrogen and oxygen. In 1800, scientists first used electricity to split water into hydrogen and oxygen gases. Today, this process, known as water electrolysis, is widely used to produce hydrogen for industrial purposes, including manufacturing ammonia for agricultural fertilizers that sustain global food production.

title: Large transformation strain of $\mathrm{Ni}_{50}\mathrm{Fe}_{23}\mathrm{Ga}_{27}$ microwires produced by the Taylor-Ulitovsky method
abstract: The martensitic transformation and associated tensile strain of $\mathrm{Ni}_{50}\mathrm{Fe}_{23}\mathrm{Ga}_{27}$ microwires produced by the Taylor--Ulitovsky method were investigated using thermomechanical analysis, electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD), and in-situ tensile X-ray diffraction (XRD). EBSD mapping at room temperature reveals cubic austenite in a nonstrained part of the microwire and tetragonal martensite in the strained part. Both EBSD and XRD show that both austenite and martensite have $[001]$ directions approximately parallel to the wire axis. The axial transformation strain calculated from the measured lattice parameters is approximately $15.4\%$. Thermal cycling under constant stresses of $20\text{--}100~\mathrm{MPa}$ reveals experimental transformation strains of $13.2\text{--}14.0\%$. Increasing tensile stress raises the transformation temperatures, with a stress--temperature slope of approximately $1.52~\mathrm{MPa}/^\circ\mathrm{C}$, comparable to that reported for $[001]$-oriented $\mathrm{Ni\text{--}Fe\text{--}Ga}$ single crystals. Overall, the observations confirm that the large macroscopic strain of up to $14.0\%$ relates to the nearly complete martensitic transformation in the microwire.

title: Thermal investigation of buffer and transition layers in AlGaN HEMT stacks
abstract: In this work, we investigate thermal transport in a set of thin-film layers used in modern HEMT designs. Our theoretical analysis employs three phonon-transport models of increasing sophistication, ranging from a relatively simple Debye-approximation model to a first-principles framework that incorporates Density Functional Theory (DFT)-derived harmonic and anharmonic phonon properties. To describe ternary semiconductors, alloy scattering is also considered, and to account for the properties of non-ideal, polycrystalline thin films, scattering at grain and film boundaries is taken into account. For modeling the specific samples at hand, the latter are fitted to thermal conductivity data measured with Time-Domain Thermoreflectance (TDTR). Overall, we find that the first-principles model performs best and produces the most physically consistent results. Special emphasis is placed on establishing a reliable procedure for determining intrinsic transport properties dominated by Umklapp scattering. Building on these, it is then possible to systematically add additional scattering terms to the models and assess how model-inherent factors, such as the treatment of scattering rates or the description of the phonon dispersion, affect model accuracy and overall predictive capabilities.

title: A Lightweight Hybrid Approach for Milling Force Reconstruction from Internal Machine Signals
abstract: Data-driven monitoring based on milling force can enable advanced manufacturing services including process optimization and condition monitoring. However, industrial implementation is often hindered by costly and intrusive hardware and large training data requirements. This paper therefore presents a hybrid approach using machine-internal signals and machining metadata to enable force-based monitoring on brownfield machines without additional sensors. Commonly available machine signals have relatively low sampling rates and cannot directly represent high-frequency milling-force variations, especially at higher spindle speeds. Instead of learning the complete force signal, which would increase model complexity, data requirements, and overfitting risk, a supervised machine-learning model predicts only the average milling force from selected machine-signal features and machining parameters. This low-frequency estimation parameterizes a static milling force model that reconstructs the force behavior over one spindle revolution. Although the static model does not reproduce all dynamic effects, it captures the force distribution, load levels, and angular regions of highest tool engagement. The approach is evaluated on one milling machine across varying process parameters, engagement conditions, cutting tools, and two workpiece materials. Dynamometer measurements are required only for development and validation. Ridge regression achieves an $R^2$ of $0.984$ and $0.991$ for average-force prediction on the test data ($\bar{F}_x$ and $\bar{F}_y$). The reconstructed force behavior over one spindle revolution achieves an $R^2$ of $0.962$ and $0.982$ ($F_x$ and $F_y$) compared with the reconstruction based on measured force features. The method provides a cost and computationally efficient basis for process monitoring, tool condition assessment, and process optimization on existing machines.

title: Alloying effects on the interface cohesion of grain boundaries in the Ni--Fe--Cr system
abstract: Grain boundaries (GBs) in polycrystalline Ni-based alloys strongly influence mechanical strength and fracture behavior, yet the effect of alloying elements such as Fe and Cr on GB cohesion remains difficult to quantify systematically. Using density functional theory (DFT), we compute rigid-body separation (RBS) curves for six symmetric-tilt Ni GBs, extracting the work of separation $W_{\mathrm{sep}}$ and maximum traction $σ_{\max}$ via the universal binding energy relation (UBER). We find that substitution of Cr or Fe into the GB plane increases both quantities relative to pure Ni GBs. To overcome the size limitations of DFT, we compare several machine-learning interatomic potential (MLIP) foundation models against the DFT dataset and identify a model achieving quantitative agreement with DFT for $W_{\mathrm{sep}}$ and $σ_{\max}$. This MLIP enables systematic sampling of alloying configurations at finer concentration steps. We show that alloying-induced changes in GB cohesion depend on both, element type and local structures, revealing trends that are inaccessible with DFT alone. Extending the analysis to a ternary $\mathrm{Ni}_{56}\mathrm{Fe}_{20}\mathrm{Cr}_{24}$ composition, inspired by the principal constituents of the widely used commercial Alloy 718, shows that the binary trends provide a useful basis for interpreting the combined effect of both substitutes, while explicit ternary calculations are required to capture their interplay quantitatively. Together, these results provide a validated workflow for quantifying the effect of alloying elements on GB cohesion in multicomponent alloys. The resulting values may serve as input for continuum-scale fracture models, paving the way toward atomistically informed multiscale modeling.

title: From AI Surrogate to Engineering Tool: Toward Production Use of Fiber-Orientation Prediction in Crash CAE
abstract: Crash simulations of glass-fiber-reinforced plastic parts are highly sensitive to the fiber-orientation field supplied to the material model. In conventional workflows, that field comes from resin-flow analysis, which requires molding-specialist support and takes about 25 hours of work per part. We previously proposed a surrogate model that addresses this bottleneck by predicting the orientation field in about 3 minutes. This paper reports the implementation, validation, and operational design that turned the model into an engineering tool for Honda design workflows. We present staged validation from 2D plates to production parts, evaluation against a predefined engineering angular-error criterion, and the expert review that approved design use in March 2025; the system has since been transferred to the crash-safety group and is in initial, limited use in directed fracture-prediction scenarios. The developed system combines injection-gate setting support for cases in which gates are unknown (90% gate-count accuracy, mean position error 11% of flow length), voxelization, surrogate inference, automatic mapping to the crash CAE model, and report generation in a single GUI. The complete orientation-preparation workflow takes about 0.1 hours, a 99.6% reduction from the conventional 25-hour flow-analysis route, and can be run directly by crash CAE engineers without molding-specialist support. As evidence of practical impact, component-level crash analysis using the predicted orientation field reduced the absolute peak-force error from 19.0% with an isotropic baseline to 11.4%, while confining predicted fracture to the test-observed region. The deployment lesson is that a surrogate model alone is not enough for practical adoption: gate-setting support, automatic data conversion, and shareable reporting are what make the model usable as a design tool.

title: Multicharged Kramers-Weyl Fermions, Quantum Geometric Hall Responses and de Haas-van Alphen Oscillations in WAl$_2$
abstract: Quantum geometry of Bloch wave functions and crystalline symmetries play a central role in condensed matter physics, shaping the electronic topology and physical responses of solids. In particular, Kramers-Weyl fermions, spin-split Fermi surfaces probed through quantum oscillations and quantum geometric nonlinear Hall and intrinsic spin Hall responses have garnered significant attention. Despite progress in understanding these phenomena individually, their coexistence with topological surface states, Fermi arcs and chirality dependent quantum geometric transport remains scarce, as pronounced responses involve suitable symmetries, SOC and Fermi surface geometry. Here, we explore this synergy in experimentally synthesized WAl$_2$, considering both structural enantiomers using first-principles calculations and symmetry analysis. We observed twelve Kramers-Weyl (KW) crossings with quantized chiral charges $|C|=1$ and $|C|=3$, accompanied by nontrivial surface states and Fermi arcs. The pronounced metallic character gives rise to six Fermi surface sheets exhibiting antisymmetric SOC, with distinct extremal orbits and candidate spin-split pairs resolved through calculated de Haas-van Alphen (dHvA) quantum oscillations. The electronic structure also exhibits large intrinsic Berry curvature dipole (BCD) arising from the asymmetric distribution of Berry curvature, giving rise to a nonlinear Hall response. The opposite structural handedness of the two enantiomers reverses the chiralities and BCD, reversing the direction of Fermi arcs and nonlinear Hall current. BCD attains $|D_{zz}|\approx0.338$, yielding nonlinear Hall current densities $|j_x|\approx5.04\times10^{10}~\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$ and $|j_y|\approx2.52\times10^{10}~\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$. We observe enhanced SHC associated with triply charged KW point at $Γ$, suggesting role of higher Chern number in the SHC.

title: Law at the Speed of AI: Critical Legal Infrastructure for the Machine Age: Autonomy Under Law Architecture (AULA)
abstract: The global deployment of autonomous AI agents within and across organisations exceeds the governance infrastructure available to constrain it. Agent communication and authentication protocols, principally the Model Context Protocol and the Agent2Agent Protocol, are maturing quickly, but maturity at the protocol layer does not produce legal legibility at the governance layer. Runtime enforcement written by the deploying organisation fixes the resources an AI agent can reach, not the authority under which it acts. Legal legibility is the capacity of a legal system to recognise, interpret and regulate activity by mapping it onto legal personhood, property, rights and liabilities. Existing (analogue) legal infrastructure cannot supply it for autonomous deployment. The resulting deficit is bidirectional. It concerns the attribution of liability when an AI agent causes harm, and the allocation of rights, including data and economic rights, generated by agentic activity and by the AI agent itself as a source of value and form of property. This paper characterises that deficit as the legal attribution gap, a material and unaddressed risk to economies, organisations and citizens that is magnified in cross-organisational multi-agent deployment. The paper describes the Autonomy Under Law Architecture (AULA), in which AI systems and data assets are registered as legal objects anchored to one or more identified legal persons, governed by cryptographically tethered smart legal instruments and evaluated at runtime. Each smart legal instrument can carry a legal context clause, through which the legislation, regulation and judicial decisions in force at the time of the act are given practical and legal effect in that evaluation. Infrastructure of this kind is a precondition for the continued function of any legal, property and economic system with both human and autonomous machine stakeholders.

title: TwinLab-Bench: Evaluating AI Scientists in Agentic Twins of Real Labs
abstract: AI agents are increasingly expected to act as AI scientists, which requires three increasingly open abilities: carrying out a given computational workflow correctly, choosing the next measurements from a given design space, and designing their own experiments. Existing benchmarks mainly evaluate the first two abilities, in a terminal or in a closed loop that selects from predefined candidates. Evaluating the third ability requires reliably executing an experiment that an agent designs, with readings grounded in a real laboratory. We introduce TwinLab-Bench, which evaluates AI scientists on self-designed experiments in 52 tasks from laboratories in the physical sciences, the life sciences, and engineering. The benchmark supports more than 100 experimental action types, and the agent's report is scored by comparison with a hidden answer taken from real laboratory records. Each task has its own TwinLab agent, an agent that serves as the environment and executes the experiments that the tested agent designs, reading the raw materials of the laboratory and calling calculators that are built from its records. Compared with a language model that sees only the task description, the TwinLab agent almost eliminates readings that deviate from the real records and inconsistent answers to a repeated request, and closed-book probes control for answers recalled from memory. We find that these tasks remain hard for frontier models: the strongest, Claude Fable 5.2, averages a score of only 45.0, and we conduct an empirical study of where it fails.

title: FastRoverVLA: Fast Vision-Language-Action Execution for Off-Road Autonomous Driving
abstract: Off-road vision-language-action (VLA) models generate scene-conditioned plans, but frequent trajectory updates can repeatedly invoke expensive multimodal inference. Reusing a prediction reduces this demand while leaving its commands exposed to changes in vehicle motion. FastRoverVLA addresses this mismatch by decoupling visual plan generation from motion-conditioned execution. Its training-free interface maintains decoded plans between visual predictions. A speed-curvature action buffer is aligned with measured motion at each update, integrated into a local trajectory, and advanced by consuming the current action. The corrected remainder is written back to the buffer, preserving motion corrections across successive updates. A bounded refresh rule normalizes speed and curvature variations within a newly decoded plan and assigns a short or long reuse budget according to the resulting plan-roughness score. The interface requires neither backbone features nor an additional learned driving policy. Over a 3 s horizon, independent real-request evaluation achieves average displacement error (ADE) and final displacement error (FDE) of 0.328/0.596 m on ORAD-3D and 0.266/0.526 m on RELLIS-3D, reducing FDE by 18.0% and 36.7% at request rates of 6.0% and 4.8%, respectively. These runs retain lower errors across four backbones and both datasets and reduce Qwen3-VL request-processing cost by factors of 16.6 and 20.8 under serial replay, while mechanism and motion-only controls identify persistent state correction as the main source of the observed accuracy benefit. The source code and evaluation materials are publicly available at https://github.com/ADEPT-ORG/FastRoverVLA.

title: Physics-Informed Feature Representations and Pretrained Tabular Foundation Models for Generalizable Melt Pool Geometry Prediction
abstract: Developing generalizable, data-efficient machine learning (ML) models for advanced manufacturing remains challenging because experimental datasets are limited and process-property relationships vary across materials and operating conditions. In laser powder bed fusion (LPBF), melt pool width, depth, and melting mode (conduction, transition, or keyhole) govern process stability and defect formation. Conventional ML models typically use dimensional process parameters, which represent laser-material interactions only implicitly and may limit cross-material transfer. This study evaluates whether two physics-informed dimensionless features, normalized enthalpy and Peclet number, combining laser processing conditions with material thermophysical properties, improve melt pool prediction over raw process parameters. We systematically benchmark seven models: four classical ML methods (Gaussian process, support vector machine, random forest, and XGBoost) and three pretrained tabular foundation models (TabPFN, TabDPT, and TabICLv2). Experiments span 316L stainless steel, IN625, IN718, and combined-material datasets, covering regression of melt pool width and depth and classification of melting modes. Dimensionless features yield comparable or superior predictive performance in most settings, with the largest gains in cross-material depth prediction (R^2 = 0.96). Tabular foundation models generally achieve stronger classification performance than classical baselines, particularly for multi-material datasets. These findings indicate that combining physically meaningful dimensionless representations with pretrained tabular models can improve data-efficient melt pool modeling and support more transferable process-window identification in LPBF.

title: Triplet adiabatic potential energy surfaces for the O($^3$P) + C$_2$(X$^1Σ_g^+$, a$^3Π_u$) reaction and quasiclassical trajectory dynamics
abstract: We present three global adiabatic potential energy surfaces (PESs) for the O($^3$P) + C$_2$(X $^1Σ_g^+$, a $^3Π_u$) to CO(X$^1Σ^+$) + C($^3$P) reaction, computed at the icMRCI+Q/aug-cc-pVTZ level. This reaction is relevant to combustion chemistry, atmospheric processes, and astrochemistry. Since the energy difference between the $^1Σ_g^+$ and $^3Π_u$ states of C$_2$ is smaller than the zero-point energy, both states mix upon interaction with the approaching O atom. Consequently, the PESs exhibit a double-well topography in the reactant valley. Beyond this feature, the three PESs display markedly different topographies. The 1 $^3A''$ PES features a deep minimum 7.16 eV below the O + C$_2$ entrance channel. In contrast, the 2 $^3A''$ and 1 $^3A'$ surfaces possess shallower collinear wells ($\approx$ 5.7 eV) and strong angular anisotropy arising from avoided crossings with higher-lying triplet states. The analytical fits reproduce the \textit{ab initio} data with root-mean-square (RMS) deviations of 0.022--0.028 eV over an energy interval exceeding 13 eV. Quasiclassical trajectory (QCT) calculations reveal higher reactivity on the barrierless $1\,^3A''$ surface compared to the $2\,^3A''$ PES, where an angle-dependent entrance barrier reduces the cross sections. Furthermore, cross sections for reactions initiated from C$_2$(X $^1Σ_g^+$) and C$_2$(a $^3Π_u$) are remarkably similar for the three PESs, regardless of the initial rovibrational state.

title: Piezocatalytic Sulfonation Enables Nongenetic Competition Therapy for Colorectal Cancer
abstract: Irreversible post-translational modifications provide a potential means to impose persistent changes in protein function, yet their controlled generation inside living cells remains challenging. Here, we develop an ultrasound-responsive potassium sodium niobate–gold (KNN@Au) piezoelectric nanoheterojunction functionalized with hyaluronic acid (KNN@Au-HA) to enable in situ terminal protein sulfonation.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: DeepChem-DEL: An Open-Source Framework for Reproducible DEL Modeling and Benchmarking
abstract: DNA-encoded libraries (DELs) allow screening of extremely large chemical spaces by tagging compounds with DNA barcodes. Machine learning (ML) techniques have enabled the extraction of meaningful chemical patterns from noisy, target-specific DEL binding data. However, existing tools for DEL machine learning (DEL-ML) remain fragmented, which limits systematic construction and reproducibility of modeling pipelines. Moreover, this fragmentation hinders integration of new models, such as chemical foundation models, into DEL workflows alongside classical approaches. To address these challenges in DEL modeling, we introduce DeepChem-DEL, an open-source suite of reproducible ML workflows for DEL modeling built on the DeepChem ecosystem. DeepChem-DEL integrates (i) a configurable denoising pipeline with (ii) modular DeepChem workflows for enrichment prediction, hit identification, and benchmarking across diverse model classes, including chemical foundation models enabled through extensions to the open-source ChemBERTa-3 framework. We evaluate DeepChem-DEL on the KinDEL and BELKA data sets, reproducing key baselines and enabling direct comparison across model classes. Our experiments demonstrate that leveraging chemical foundation models yields performance competitive with, and in several cases exceeding, previously explored approaches such as graph convolutional networks and random forest models. Together, these results demonstrate that DeepChem-DEL is a scalable and extensible platform for DEL-ML, while highlighting the potential of chemical foundation models for improved DEL modeling and prioritization.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Reward misalignment as an opportunity for materials discovery
abstract: Reward misalignment is usually regarded as a failure of artificial intelligence. In materials discovery with generative AI models, however, disagreement between predefined rewards and expert judgment may reveal materials that the rewards overlook. We investigate this possibility using electronic flat bands as a prime example. Experts mostly agree with a numerical bandwidth score, but their disagreements are systematic and cannot be explained by an estimated 5% rate of mistaken labels. We learn the experts' preferences from pairwise comparisons and use them to guide a crystal diffusion model. The learned preferences and numerical score agree on the flattest bands but diverge elsewhere. For example, the preferences favor KCo2As2 and CoGa, reported compounds with partially flat bands that the score would discard. The framework also extends to synthesizability and phonon properties. Our findings suggest that reward misalignment can expose opportunities for materials discovery beyond what fixed rewards are designed to find.

title: Thermodynamically Consistent Neural Networks for a Universal Fluid Gibbs Free Energy Equation of State
abstract: Over the past three centuries, many thermodynamics researchers have worked to develop fluid equations of state with both high accuracy and broad applicability, proposing various theoretical frameworks and models. Building on these efforts, this study uses Gibbs free energy as the starting point and introduces thermodynamically consistent neural networks to construct a fluid equation of state based on Gibbs free energy (GEoS). This approach establishes a novel machine learning framework that provides a unified representation of fluid states. GEoS performs well on the vapor- and liquid-phase density test sets, with average absolute relative deviations (AARDs) of 5.25% and 3.96%, respectively. It outperforms conventional volume-translated cubic equations of state and existing machine learning models, demonstrating its effectiveness. Further analysis using the UMAP dimensionality reduction method shows that most molecules in the test set belong to extrapolation systems, confirming the strong generalization ability of the model. Finally, the test results show that the PC-SAFT equation fitted using GEoS maintains high predictive accuracy, providing a reliable basis for its practical application in industry.

title: Dual Action of Electrolyte Additives in High-Voltage Li-Ion Cells
abstract: Electrolyte additives have outsized effects on cell performance, but determining their mechanism of action can be difficult. Here, we evaluate whether simple electrochemical tests can reveal which electrode (cathode, anode or both) is targeted by specific additives. Our experiments quantified the rates of reductive and oxidative side-reactions in NMC532 vs. graphite cells containing 12 different electrolyte formulations. We found that gains in interphasial stability were highly correlated, with successful additives decreasing both types of side-reactions by similar magnitude. This dual action could be indicative of the role of crosstalk on cell degradation, as soluble species formed on one electrode can decompose at the other end of the cell. Although electrochemical tests are insufficient for understanding mechanisms of improvement, they can reveal interesting effects that complement other characterization tools.

title: Sliding-ferroelectric control of dipolar and quadrupolar excitons in R-stacked WSe$_2$
abstract: A fundamental property of interlayer excitons is their dipolar character, enabling electrical tunability, enhanced exciton-exciton interactions and extended lifetime. It is important for studying collective phenomena and realizing novel optoelectronic devices. However, in homo- or heterostructures based on two-dimensional semiconductors, the magnitude and orientation of the dipole moment are commonly locked due to spatially confined charges and nature of the band transition. Here, we use gate-dependent photoluminescence of few-layer R-WSe2 to harness sliding ferroelectricity for controlling the exciton dipole configuration of emerging layer-hybridised excitons. The sliding-ferroelectric control enables a pronounced on/off switching of the diffusive transport of hybrid dipolar excitons, while further facilitating gradual and abrupt dipole reconfigurations with emerging quadrupolar excitons. Our optical probe reveals intermediate states of vertically aligned interfacial polarisation with magnitudes that confirm cumulative polarisation in multilayers. Overall, our work presents sliding ferroelectricity as a powerful tool to tune interlayer coupling and layer hybridisation. These results represent a step toward ferroelectric-controlled exciton interconnects and novel multi-bit optical memories.

title: Unusual increase in electrical and thermal conductivity of severely deformed CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy: Roles of disordering and nanostructuring in electron and phonon transport
abstract: This work investigates how defect engineering and nanostructuring via severe plastic deformation influence electrical and thermal transport in the high-entropy alloy CrMnFeCoNi. High-pressure torsion (HPT) for up to N = 4 turns produces a hierarchical defect structure, including deformation twins at low strains, dislocations and Lomer-Cottrell locks at intermediate strains, and a high fraction of high-angle grain boundaries at large strains. While hardness naturally increases and saturates at ~520 Hv, both electrical and thermal conductivity exhibit an unusual increase upon HPT processing (from 0.953 MS m-1 and 10.3 W m-1 K-1 after homogenization to 1.003 +- 0.005 MS m-1 and 14.4 W m-1 K-1 after N = 4). Analysis based on the Wiedemann-Franz law indicates a modest increase in electron transport (~5%) and a significant increase in phonon transport (~100%) after HPT processing. The phonon mean free path remains small on the order of 0.6-1.1 nm, and comparison with the Cahill-Pohl model shows that heat transport occurs near the minimum thermal conductivity limit, where vibrational modes are strongly scattered. This suggests that the enhancement in thermal transport is not governed by conventional defect scattering, but it is hypothesized that modifications in atomic-scale disorder, such as deformation-induced short-range ordering, are responsible for this unusual behavior. Specific heat capacity increases after HPT, consistent with stored defect energy. The linear thermal expansion exhibits a non-monotonic behavior, decreasing initially due to internal stresses and relaxation effects, and increasing at higher strains due to grain boundary-induced anharmonicity. These findings highlight the complex interplay between defects, atomic-scale disorder, and nanostructure in governing the electrical and thermal properties of severely deformed high-entropy alloys via electron and phonon scattering.

title: Multi-Layer Functional Metabolomics Reveals Chemical Interactions Between the Plant-Associated Bacterium Serratia marcescens and Phytophthora
abstract: Oomycete pathogens of the genus Phytophthora cause devastating crop losses worldwide, highlighting the need for novel biocontrol agents. Here, we developed a multi-layer functional metabolomics workflow that incorporates an LC-MS/MS-based metal infusion assay in combination with microfractionation-based bioassays against Phytophthora infestans and metal-binding assays to map bioactivity from Serratia marcescens extracts. MS/MS analysis and feature-based molecular networking supported the annotation of activity-associated metabolites, including prodigiosin, serratiochelins, and an uncharacterized putative serratiochelin analog designated serratiochelin G. Complementary chrome azurol S assays and post-column iron infusion provided evidence of iron-binding properties. Comparative genomic analysis and L-lysine supplementation supported a proposed biosynthetic origin of serratiochelin G involving cadaverine incorporation. This workflow enables metabolite prioritization by integrating non-targeted LC-MS/MS with chromatographically resolved bioactivity and complementary functional assays.

title: A Machine-Learning Framework Integrating Frequency-Domain Spectral Features for Ligand Classification and Candidate Prioritization
abstract: AI-assisted drug discovery (AIDD) combines molecular modeling with machine learning to support lead identification and candidate prioritization. Conventional molecular descriptors principally encode static chemical structures, leaving frequency-domain behavior as an additional source of molecular information. We therefore developed the terahertz fusion descriptor (THz-FD), a feature-fusion framework that integrates terahertz (THz) frequency-domain features for Na+/K+-ATPase ligand classification and retrospective ranking. Extra Trees (ET), Random Forest (RF), and support vector machine (SVM) classifiers were evaluated under repeated-stratified, Molecule_Key-grouped, and scaffold-grouped cross-validation. In repeated-stratified validation, the combined representation achieved mean macro-averaged area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values of 0.8538, 0.8423, and 0.8480 for ET, RF, and SVM models, respectively. Adding the model-derived fragment integral spectrum descriptor (FISD) features and protein-reference context features produced absolute macro-AUC changes of -0.0014, -0.0011, and +0.0016 for ET, RF, and SVM, respectively, and absolute macro-F1 changes of +0.0017, +0.0049, and +0.0090. None of the 27 paired comparisons reached statistical significance after Benjamini-Hochberg correction. Molecular docking and quantum-chemical calculations provided auxiliary structural and vibrational context for the selected ligands. These findings establish THz-FD as a traceable framework for integrating frequency-domain information with conventional descriptors in ligand-activity modeling and target-specific drug screening.

title: Interpretable machine learning of formation energies and band gaps in hybrid perovskites through SHAP analysis and SISSO modelling
abstract: Accurate and interpretable property prediction is essential for exploring hybrid organic–inorganic perovskites. Here, we combine machine-learning screening with SHAP analysis and SISSO descriptor discovery. Using 4,456 compounds, optimized XGBoost models achieved test-set $R^2$ values of 0.99 for formation energy and 0.93 for band gap and were applied to over 180,000 candidates.
